headline: ACC writes to 41 banks over ৳276 crore embezzlement
summary: The Anti-Corruption Commission has sought information from 41 banks regarding the alleged misappropriation of CSR funds for the Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman Memorial Trust.
details: The Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) has sent letters to 41 scheduled banks seeking information regarding a case involving the embezzlement of ৳276 crore from Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) funds.
// a case involving the embezzlement of ৳276 crore from Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) funds. The funds were allegedly misappropriated for the Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman Memorial Trust.

The accused in the case include ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, her sister Sheikh Rehana, and Nazrul Islam Majumder, the former president of the Bangladesh Association of Banks (BAB) and former chairman of Exim Bank.
According to the case's first information report (FIR), Sheikh Hasina served as the president and Sheikh Rehana as the vice-president of the Memorial Trust.
The FIR alleges that the duo established the trust for 'dishonest purposes of personal gain' and used their influence through the BAB to collect funds from the banks' CSR budgets.
The ACC stated that it has reviewed records and information obtained from 41 scheduled banks in Bangladesh as part of its ongoing investigation into the matter.

headline_marked: Crude bombs explode in [[house in Chapainawabganj]], damaging structure
headline: Crude bombs explode in house in Chapainawabganj, damaging structure
summary: Police suspect around 15 crude bombs were stored underground at the residence of Mohammad Yahia, whose family has since fled the scene.
details: A series of crude bombs exploded at a house in Chapainawabganj Sadar upazila last night, causing significant damage to the building and triggering panic among neighbors.
According to Mohammad Ekramul Hossain, officer-in-charge of Sadar Model Police Station, the bombs were allegedly stored underground at the house of Mohammad Yahia.
Local residents reported hearing a series of loud explosions around 8:30 PM, after which they discovered the house had been damaged.
Law enforcement agencies arrived at the spot shortly after the incident to begin an investigation into the cause of the explosions.
Chapainawabganj Additional Superintendent of Police ANM Wasim Firoz stated that everyone in the house had fled the scene before police arrived.
Police are currently investigating whether the house owner, Mohammad Yahia, or his family has any political or criminal links.
The authorities are working to determine exactly how the bombs were stored and what triggered the series of blasts.
caption:
A series of crude bombs exploded inside a house in Chapainawabganj, leaving the building damaged and the residents fleeing.

A series of crude bombs exploded at a house in Chapainawabganj Sadar upazila last night, causing significant damage to the building and triggering panic among neighbors.

According to Mohammad Ekramul Hossain, officer-in-charge of Sadar Model Police Station, the bombs were allegedly stored underground at the house of Mohammad Yahia.

Local residents reported hearing a series of loud explosions around 8:30 PM, after which they discovered the house had been damaged.

Law enforcement agencies arrived at the spot shortly after the incident to begin an investigation into the cause of the explosions.

Chapainawabganj Additional Superintendent of Police ANM Wasim Firoz stated that everyone in the house had fled the scene before police arrived.

Police are currently investigating whether the house owner, Mohammad Yahia, or his family has any political or criminal links.

The authorities are working to determine exactly how the bombs were stored and what triggered the series of blasts.
